prompt: What problem with `public` did modules set out to solve?
hint: A library is several packages.

choices.text: `public` classes were slower to load than package-private ones, and modules sped them up
choices.why: Access levels have nothing to do with loading speed.

choices.text: A class public to its library's other packages was public to everybody
choices.why: Right: nothing could say "public to my own packages, private to the rest".

choices.text: `public` could not be used on interfaces
choices.why: Interfaces have been `public` since Java 1.0.

prompt: In `module-info.java`, the keyword that makes a package visible to other modules is `___`.
hint: The library used it once, for its `api` package.

prompt: `Shortcut` imported `com.example.library.internal.Index`. What did `javac` answer?
hint: The package was on disk, compiled a moment earlier.

choices.text: A warning that the package is internal, and it compiled
choices.why: It was an error, two of them, and nothing compiled.

choices.text: `Index is not public in com.example.library.internal`
choices.why: `Index` is `public`; the module, not the class, is what refused.

choices.text: `package com.example.library.internal does not exist`
choices.why: Right: to the app module an unexported package is not there at all.

choices.text: A `module not found` error for `com.example.library`
choices.why: The module was found and `Main` compiled against it; only the package was refused.

prompt: `jar --describe-module` printed `requires java.base mandated`, and nobody wrote that line. Why is it there?
hint: Where do `String` and `Object` live?

choices.text: Every module depends on `java.base`, so it is added to every declaration
choices.why: Right: `mandated` means the language put it there.

choices.text: `jar` copied it from the app module's `requires`
choices.why: The app module requires `com.example.library`, not `java.base`.

choices.text: `Index` uses `Map`, and `jar` scanned the bytecode for it
choices.why: Even a module using nothing at all gets the line; `jar` did not scan anything.

prompt: Match each piece to what it does.
hint: Section 02 used all four.

pairs.right: says which modules this one needs
says which packages others may use
tells `javac` where each module's sources are
tells `java` where to find compiled modules

right_distractors: opens a package to reflection for one run

prompt: `java --module-path out -m com.example.app/com.example.app.Main` names a module and a class. What does the part before the slash tell the JVM?
hint: On the module path, every class belongs to a module.

choices.text: The directory under `out` where the class file lives
choices.why: It happens to match the directory here, and it is the module's name, read from `module-info.class`.

choices.text: Which module to start from, and so which `requires` to resolve
choices.why: Right: the JVM resolves that module's dependencies before running anything.

choices.text: The package of the class, written in the module syntax
choices.why: The package is `com.example.app` inside the class's full name, after the slash.

prompt: `Peek` failed on the module path before it ever reached `setAccessible`. Where, and why?
hint: Read the frame from `Peek` and the end of the message.

choices.text: At `Class.forName`, because unexported classes cannot even be loaded
choices.why: `forName` succeeded; the trace points at `newInstance`, on line 11.

choices.text: Building an `Index`: its package is not exported to the app module
choices.why: Right: `IllegalAccessException ... does not export com.example.library.internal to module com.example.app`.

choices.text: Reading `titles`, because a `Map` cannot be copied into a `TreeMap`
choices.why: The copy worked fine on the next run, once the package was opened.

prompt: Why does the section call `--add-opens` a deliberate escape hatch rather than a loophole?
hint: Who types it, and where?

choices.text: It only works on Java 17 and later
choices.why: When it works is not the point; who has to write it down is.

choices.text: It opens a package for good, so it is used once and forgotten
choices.why: It opens for one run only, and has to be given again every time.

choices.text: The flag names the module, package and reader at start-up
choices.why: Right: a reach into somebody's internals is visible to whoever runs it, not hidden in code.

prompt: The same `Peek`, run with `java -cp out/com.example.library:out/com.example.app`, printed the map with no flag. Why?
hint: What happens to `module-info.class` on the class path?

choices.text: On the class path, module declarations are ignored
choices.why: Right: modules only bind code that runs as modules, so every package is open.

choices.text: The class path keeps the `--add-opens` from the previous run
choices.why: Each JVM starts fresh; nothing carries over from an earlier run.

choices.text: `TreeMap` bypasses the module check
choices.why: The check was on building `Index`, before any `TreeMap` existed.

prompt: `Bytes` ran on the class path, with no module of its own, and still got `InaccessibleObjectException`. What refused it?
hint: Whose package was it reaching into?

choices.text: The unnamed module, which closes the class path to reflection since Java 17
choices.why: The unnamed module is where `Bytes` lives, and it is open; the refusal came from the other side.

choices.text: `java.base`, which does not open `java.lang`
choices.why: Right: the JDK's own modules keep their internals closed, to everybody.

choices.text: The source launcher, which forbids `setAccessible` in programs run from source
choices.why: Compiled and run with `javac` and `java`, it fails the same way.

choices.text: `String.value` is `final`, and final fields cannot be made accessible
choices.why: Final fields of your own classes can be; the message names the module, not the modifier.

prompt: Every class on the class path belongs to the ___ module.
hint: `Bytes`'s error named it.

prompt: How many modules did `java --list-modules` report for the installed JDK?
hint: `wc -l` counted them.

prompt: How did `jlink` decide which JDK modules to put in `image`?
hint: It was given one module.

choices.text: It ran the program and recorded which classes were loaded
choices.why: `jlink` runs nothing; it reads declarations.

choices.text: It copied the modules `jdeps` had printed
choices.why: `jdeps` was a separate command; `jlink` needs no report from it.

choices.text: It followed every `requires` from the app module down to `java.base`
choices.why: Right: three modules, because those are all the declarations reach.

choices.text: It took every module of the JDK and compressed them
choices.why: The image listed three modules, not 69.

prompt: `du` measured `image` at 60M and the JDK at 331M. Roughly how many times smaller is the image? Give a whole number.
hint: Divide the larger by the smaller.

prompt: A colleague wants `jlink` to build a small runtime for a class-path service with forty library jars, none of them modules. What does the section say?
hint: `jlink` needs `requires` lines to know where to stop.

choices.text: Pass the forty jars to `--add-modules` and `jlink` converts them
choices.why: `jlink` links modules; it does not turn plain jars into modules.

choices.text: Not the application; only a JDK trimmed to what `jdeps` reports
choices.why: Right: name the JDK modules by hand with `--add-modules`, and keep the jars on the class path.

choices.text: It works, because the class path is the unnamed module and `jlink` accepts it
choices.why: The unnamed module has no name to `--add-modules` and no `requires` to follow.

prompt: Which of these are costs of making an application modular, according to section 05? Choose all that apply.
hint: Dependencies, frameworks and two paths.

choices.text: Every dependency has to be a module, or pass for one
choices.why: Yes: the application is only as modular as its least modular jar.

choices.text: Packages that frameworks reflect into have to be declared `opens`
choices.why: Yes: the declaration fills up with exceptions to its own rule.

choices.text: The program runs more slowly on the module path
choices.why: Speed is not among the costs the section names.

choices.text: `javac` can no longer compile it with `--release`
choices.why: `--release` works for modules as for anything else.

prompt: A module `requires` a library that is missing from the module path. When does the program find out?
hint: Resolution happens before anything runs.

choices.text: The first time a class from the library is used, maybe an hour into a run
choices.why: That is the class path's way, with `NoClassDefFoundError`; a module fails earlier.

choices.text: At start-up, before `main` runs
choices.why: Right: the JVM resolves every `requires` first and refuses to start without them.

choices.text: Never: missing modules are skipped and their calls return null
choices.why: Nothing is skipped; a missing module is a refusal to start.

prompt: For an ordinary application, what does the lesson recommend?
hint: As every other lesson of the course has done.

choices.text: A `module-info.java` from the first day, so it never has to be added later
choices.why: That is the cost section 05 lists, paid for a benefit an application often does not need.

choices.text: The class path
choices.why: Right: modules pay off for a published library or a self-contained runtime.

choices.text: `--add-opens` for every package, to avoid surprises
choices.why: That is an escape hatch for one reach, not a way to build an application.

prompt: You upgrade the JDK under a service, and it now fails at start-up with `module java.base does not "opens java.util" to unnamed module`. The service has no `module-info.java`. What is the likely cause, and the fix?
hint: Section 03's last paragraph.

choices.text: The service must now be made modular, with a `module-info.java` of its own at the root
choices.why: Making it modular would not change what the library reflects into.

choices.text: A library reflects into `java.util`: upgrade it; `--add-opens` meanwhile
choices.why: Right: the JDK's own wall, met by class-path code; `--add-opens java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED` is the stopgap.

choices.text: The new JDK is missing `java.util`; reinstall it
choices.why: `java.util` is in `java.base`, which every JDK has; the message says it is closed, not absent.

prompt: Put the steps of section 04, from source to a runtime of its own, in order.
hint: Compile before you link, link before you run.
items: `jdeps -s` shows what the app module depends on
